topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecture and outlines its learning objectives.

topics.label: Viral origins of cancer genetics and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays used to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer-driving genes and explore their molecular mechanisms through cell cycle control and mutation dosage effects.

topics.label: Types and mechanisms of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the origins and cellular consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability arising from defective DNA repair pathways and mitotic failure.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential mutation accumulation drives tumor progression in sporadic cancers and hereditary predisposition syndromes.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section concludes the lecture, invites questions, and recommends further reading.
